terms.gloss: the condition of the body, physique
evidence: Cic. Brut. 64: quī nōn tam habitūs corporis opīmōs quam gracilitātēs cōnsectentur (Lewis & Short s.v. habitus)
terms.comment: “The way the body holds itself”: bonī (malī) habitūs esse or in bonō (malō) habitū esse, to be in good (bad) shape (Traupman 65); corporis habitūs excellentis, in excellent shape (Traupman 62).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 62, 63, 65, 295, 377, checked against the searchable text of the book.
